reasoning_summary:
Step 0005 (fix two perfect matchings M, M' of the tree T) is unobjectionable; if T has fewer than two perfect matchings the claim is immediate. Step 0006 carries the whole argument and holds. Since M, M' are subsets of E(T), the graph G = (V, M union M') is a subgraph of T. Every vertex of G has degree 1 or 2: degree at least 1 because M (indeed each of M, M') covers every vertex, and degree at most 2 because at most one M-edge and one M'-edge meet any vertex. Maximum degree 2 forces each component of G to be a path or a cycle. A path component with at least two edges is impossible: its endpoint v has degree 1, so its unique incident edge vu must belong to both M and M' (each matching must cover v, and vu is the only available edge); then u is already covered by both M and M' through vu, so any second edge at u lies in neither M nor M', contradicting u having degree 2 inside the path. Hence every component of G is either a single edge belonging to M intersect M' or a cycle. T is acyclic and G is a subgraph of T, so no cycle component occurs, so every edge of M union M' lies in M intersect M', i.e. M = M'. This is exactly the author's chain of reasoning, and it terminates correctly.

The proof does contain one wording defect: the author writes that a component is 'an isolated vertex (which is in M and M')', but a component cannot be an isolated vertex, since a perfect matching gives every vertex degree at least 1 in G. The intended object is an isolated edge, as the parenthetical 'which is in M and M'' confirms (membership in a matching is a property of edges, not vertices). This is a slip in naming the object rather than an unjustified inference: the dichotomy the author appeals to (shared single edge, or cycle) is the correct dichotomy, is validly derived from 'M and M' cover all vertices' as the author says, and is applied correctly against the acyclicity of T. The author also leaves the path-exclusion sub-argument implicit, but the assertion is true and follows directly from the covering condition he cites, so this is a level-of-detail matter rather than a gap that can fail. No step admits a counterexample, so the verdict is VALID and the counterexample field is empty as required.
